bull.b: CAVA is demonstrating broad-based demand through both sales growth and higher guest traffic, reducing reliance on price or mix alone. Sustained comparable-store momentum can support operating leverage, improve returns on new locations, and provide a durable foundation for continued expansion.

The combination of rapid restaurant growth, strong average unit volumes, and new-restaurant productivity above 100% indicates that CAVA has a repeatable expansion model. Productive openings can compound the store base and extend brand reach while supporting future revenue growth.

A cash-rich, debt-free position gives CAVA meaningful flexibility to fund restaurant openings, operational investments, and working-capital needs internally. The available revolver adds further resilience, allowing growth initiatives to continue without immediate dependence on external financing.

bear.b: Rising food, packaging, labor, and delivery-related costs are already reducing restaurant-level margin, while management expects additional pressure in the second half. If these costs persist, sales growth may translate less efficiently into earnings and cash generation.

bear.t: Thin And Declining Free Cash Flow
bear.b: Although operations generate positive cash, relatively modest free cash flow indicates that reported earnings are not yet converting efficiently after investment requirements. Weakening conversion could constrain internally funded expansion and make cash generation more sensitive to operating or development spending.

CAVA has moved into profitability, but the sharp variation in net margin shows that earnings quality and operating leverage are not yet fully consistent. Continued volatility can make results less predictable and leaves the business more exposed to cost inflation, investment cycles, and seasonal effects.
